summary: Defines the multipart/report MIME type, a container for email reports of any kind. Only its use for delivery status reports is specified here, but the aim is for all report types to share one format. It was replaced by RFC 3462.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1892 defines a MIME container for mail system reports. It includes a part for people, a part for software, and may include the original message to help diagnose a problem.

subtitle: A MIME container for human-readable and machine-readable mail reports.

tldr.problem: Mail programs need to recognize and process administrative reports separately from ordinary mail.
tldr.mechanism: Multipart/Report contains a human-readable part, a machine-readable report part, and optionally the returned message or part of it.

today: RFC 1892 was obsoleted by RFC 3462, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: The Multipart/Report Type
sections.content: Multipart/Report is a MIME content type for electronic mail reports. In this memo it is specified for delivery status reports, though the RFC notes that a single report type can serve reports of different kinds. It must be the top-level content type so user agents and gateways can identify a report automatically.
sections.plainLanguage: The outer content type labels an email as a report. Mail software can use that label to recognize and process it.

sections.title: The Report Body Parts
sections.content: A Multipart/Report body has two or three parts in a fixed order. The first, required part is a human-readable explanation. The second, required part gives a machine-parsable account of the event. An optional third part contains the returned message or a portion of it, which may help experts diagnose a problem.
sections.plainLanguage: The report has an explanation for a person and structured details for software. It may also include some or all of the original message.

sections.title: Returning Message Headers
sections.content: The Text/RFC822-Headers content type labels the headers of a failed message without returning the complete message. It contains all header lines before the blank line, including MIME-Version and MIME Content headers. The RFC says these headers are useful for identifying the failed message and diagnosing it.
sections.plainLanguage: A report can return just the original message's headers. These are the lines before the blank line that separates the headers from the body.
